text_blocks.snippet: A stroke can lead to a wide range of physical, cognitive, and emotional consequences, some temporary and others permanent. These effects vary greatly depending on the stroke's severity, location in the brain, and the individual's overall health.
snippet_highlighted_words: a wide range of physical, cognitive, and emotional consequences, some temporary and others permanent

list.snippet: Motor Impairment: Weakness or paralysis on one side of the body (hemiparesis or hemiplegia) is common, affecting movement, coordination, and balance.
Sensory Changes: Numbness, tingling, or altered sensations on one side of the body are possible.
Speech and Language Problems: Difficulty speaking (aphasia) or understanding language, as well as problems with swallowing (dysphagia) can occur.
